categories.main_business_segments: Ohashi Technica operates primarily in two business segments: automotive-related parts (including engine components, body assembly parts, brake parts, and EV-related components) and other related parts. The company is a global supplier, engaging in manufacturing, sales, technical development, and logistics for these segments, with a strong focus on the automotive industry.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary technologies such as press-fit projection joining, precision plastic forming, precision press processing, and advanced joining techniques. It also utilizes precision cold forging technology and collaborates with suppliers for joint development, aiming for high-strength, high-precision, lightweight, and compact components, especially for electrified vehicle applications.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Ohashi Technica serves major automotive manufacturers (OEMs) and automotive parts suppliers globally, with a particular emphasis on Japanese automakers and their global operations. The company also supplies parts to OA/AV equipment manufacturers and other industrial sectors, but automotive customers represent the overwhelming majority of its business.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company has a global footprint with operations in Japan, the Americas (USA, Mexico), China, ASEAN (mainly Thailand), Europe (UK), and Taiwan. It maintains manufacturing and sales subsidiaries in each of these regions, supporting customers' global production needs.
categories.supply_chain_position: Ohashi Technica operates as a midstream supplier, providing both factory (in-house manufacturing) and fabless (outsourced manufacturing) functions. It acts as a key Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier, delivering finished and semi-finished components to automotive OEMs and major parts manufacturers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening four core functions: development (especially for EV/HEV components), manufacturing (expanding in-house production and automation), procurement (deepening supplier collaboration and pursuing M&A), and global operations (establishing multi-regional manufacturing capabilities). R&D focuses on advancing proprietary joining and forming technologies, supporting electrification, and contributing to CO2 reduction and ESG initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of automotive and industrial parts, both manufactured in-house and procured from partners. Revenue is recognized upon delivery to customers, with most payments received within four months of shipment. There are no significant recurring or subscription-based revenue streams.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Ohashi Technica competes with other global automotive parts suppliers, particularly those specializing in precision metal components and joining technologies. While specific competitors are not named, the company positions itself as a trusted, indispensable supplier to major automakers, leveraging its dual factory/fabless model and global reach.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥40.0 billion, with operating profit of ¥1.78 billion and net profit attributable to parent shareholders of ¥1.52 billion. The company has demonstrated steady growth in sales and profits, with a strong balance sheet (equity ratio over 80%) and a global workforce of 736 employees. The mid-term plan targets ¥45 billion in sales and ¥4.15 billion in operating profit by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Ohashi Technica emphasizes its ability to deliver high-quality, high-precision, and innovative components that are essential for advanced vehicle manufacturing, especially in the era of electrification. Its unique value lies in proprietary joining and forming technologies, a flexible global supply network, and a dual factory/fabless model that enables both cost competitiveness and technical differentiation.
